newsitem.title: USA: Small emerging fund has big returns in 96 - Micropal.
newsitem.headline: Small emerging fund has big returns in 96 - Micropal.

text.p: Korea Small Companies Trust, a tiny $2 million fund, was the top performing emerging market fund of 1996 with a total return of 168.95 percent, according to Micropal's February issue of Emerging Market Fund Monitor.

"This was quite an achievement considering the fund targeted companies in a country whose stock market was one of the worst performers of the year," said David Masters, associate editor of the Emerging Market Fund Monitor.
Masters said one stock was responsible for the tiny Korean fund's performance as its value skyrocketed during its initial public offering on the Korean Stock Exchange.
"Ironically, the fund's success appears to be leading to its ultimate demise," said Masters.
He noted that many of the fund's investors cashed in their profits, causing the fund's assets under management to sink to about $2 million from $24 million.
Masters said investors probably did not wish "to find out whether the fund manager's choice of holdings was due to pure luck or to adept stockpicking skills."
Russian and Eastern European funds dominated the remaining top ten positions in their 1996 rankings, Micropal said.
Regent Pacific Group's Russian equity fund, White Tiger Investment Co, scored the number two slot, returning 150.46 percent in 1996.
Rounding out the top five for the year were Firebird Fund LP, up 145.61 percent, Mercury ST Eastern European Fund, up 137.95 percent and Blue Tiger Investment Co, up 137.53 percent.
The survey uses U.S. dollar returns, net-asset-value to net-asset-value, and gross income is reinvested for the period ending December 31, Micropal said.
